3C.2 Christians commanded to love one another as Christ has loved you.
21B.12 A servant is not above or greater than his master.

precepts.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, the servant is not greater than his lord. Christ was the example, and we are going to walk the same footsteps; you are going to get punished the same way. It is not going to be easy; it is not supposed to be easy. If our Lord and Master went through it, do you not think that you are going to go through it? If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
precepts.point: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. And there is a period at the end of that. Nothing should be able to separate you, because you know what is at the end of this: paradise is waiting on us. You are being put in a furnace to be tried and turned into pure gold. Your wicked family turning their back on you? Good. When I came in this truth I got rid of a whole lot of dead weight and useless conversations; the only people that call me now call about the truth. If it is not about the scriptures, do not talk to me; that is beneficial for me and for you.
precepts.why:
Romans 8 says, “He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?” The Most High is trying to give us a kingdom. Christ went through the furnace, and he is doing the same thing with us. We are the ambassadors of Christ: do you think you are not going to go through the same thing? Do you think you are not going to be punished? Yes, you are.

Christ said it himself: “For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.” Christ was the example, and we are going to walk the same footsteps. We will be punished the same way he was.

It is not going to be easy, and it is not supposed to be easy. If our Lord and Master went through it, do you not think that you are going to go through it? Do you not think that you deserve to go through it?

“If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.” Knowing that the servant walks where his lord walked, we take the fire as the way to be fixed. That is why all things work together for good to them that love God: the trials are the furnace Christ went through first, and the kingdom is at the end of it.

precepts.text: The devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray him. He put the thought in Judas's heart and Judas acted on it.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.text: A new commandment: that ye love one another as I have loved you; by this shall all men know ye are my disciples. Repeated in John 15:17.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Where did John get this “new commandment”? From Christ: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.”

Christ said it to the disciples, and John repeated it in his epistle. Christ said it over and over again: “These things I command you, that ye love one another.”

That is why John can say in the same breath, “I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning”, and then, “Again, a new commandment I write unto you”. It is old because it came from Moses' time. It is called new because Israel was not following it. Going back to Moses, we were children in whom is no faith, rebellious; we waxed fat and kicked.

So the mark of Christ's disciples is love one to another, among our own people. “He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.” The one who despises his brother and his people will stumble, and stumble in a lot of deep but basic things.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another”. Christ gives us the commandment to love each other. That's unity. “as I have loved you”. The same way he loves you, he wants you to love one another. “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples”. How will they know you're his disciple? “if ye have love one to another.” By loving each other.

If you don't show love to another brother, you're not Christ's disciple. You're Satan's disciple. Everybody running their mouth showing hatred is Satan's disciple, not Christ's. Loving each other is how people tell the difference.
